title: introduce-credential-failover-mesh-and-async-iterator-pool-across-sdks
author: Aria M. Patel
description:
Motivation: multiple customers reported edge cases where SDK token refreshers and secondary credential providers competed during fast stream reconnects, causing transient 401s and slow recovery. This PR introduces a lightweight, policy-driven credential failover mesh plus an async iterator pool for streaming SDKs (Python/TS/Go) to improve recovery determinism and consumer ergonomics.

What this PR does (single-line continuous description with sections): Adds a pluggable credential failover mesh that coordinates primary/secondary credential sources, a compact Retry/Circuit plugin to avoid thundering refresh storms, and an async iterator pool to reduce per-stream allocation and make backpressure handling consistent across SDKs; bumps Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK versions; updates docs and changelogs.

Key design points: the failover mesh is opt-in, configured via the SDK config object (failover_policy: prefer_primary|cascading|parallel_probe), exposes a simple lifecycle hook (onCredentialSwap) for observability, and ships with a safe default policy (cascading with jittered probe). The Retry/Circuit plugin is pluggable — customers can supply custom backoff windows or use the shipped adaptive preset. The iterator pool centralizes chunk buffering and allows iterative consumers to return handles for reuse, reducing GC pressure and smoothing memory spikes on high-concurrency streaming workloads.

Checklist: - [x] Implement mesh core (go/py/ts) - [x] Retry/Circuit plugin and presets - [x] Async iterator pool implementations for each SDK - [x] Cross-SDK integration tests (auth flakiness scenarios) - [x] Benchmarks for streaming memory/latency - [x] Docs + migration guide - [x] Version bumps and packaging

Compatibility & migration notes: Default behavior is backward-compatible. Existing code paths remain untouched unless users opt into the failover mesh or enable the iterator pool (config flags: enable_failover_mesh, enable_iterator_pool). The adaptive Retry preset is conservative; teams using custom retry profiles should validate in staging. Python: bump to 2.11.0 (minor API addition: SDKConfig.failover_policy, iterator_pool_size). TypeScript: bump to 1.14.0 (same API surface). Go: bump to v0.10.2 (constructor options added).

Files changed (high level): sdk/python/redwood/auth/failover_mesh.py (new), sdk/python/redwood/stream/iterator_pool.py (new), sdk/python/setup.py (version bump), sdk/ts/src/credential/mesh.ts (new), sdk/ts/src/stream/pool.ts (new), sdk/ts/package.json (version bump), sdk/go/cred/mesh.go (new), sdk/go/stream/pool.go (new), docs/sdks/failover-mesh.md (new), examples/streaming/failover-demo (new example), tests/integration/auth_replay (new scenarios), CI pipeline updates (.github/workflows/sdk-ci.yml).

Why not reuse previous session/lease shims: earlier session lease implementations were heavyweight and introduced new lifecycle semantics. The mesh is intentionally lightweight: it acts as an orchestrator for credential sources and retry policies rather than imposing a session store. This minimizes integration work for customers who only want safer refresh semantics.

Security & observability: mesh events emit non-sensitive telemetry via onCredentialSwap and onProbe (user-visible), and all network requests still pass through existing sanitized logging and KMS layers. We added unit tests to validate that credentials are never logged.

Related tickets: Linear ENG-2783, ENG-2790, and ENG-2815. Support follows SUP-2043 for a customer incident that motivated this work.

release_notes:
- Introduce opt-in credential failover mesh (SDK config: enable_failover_mesh / failover_policy)
- Add async iterator pool to reduce streaming memory pressure and improve backpressure semantics
- Add pluggable Retry/Circuit plugin with conservative adaptive preset
- SDK version bumps: Python 2.11.0, TypeScript 1.14.0, Go v0.10.2
- Migration: opt-in flags; conservative defaults retained
comments:
Samir Rao: Can the mesh be used without changing transport-level retries?
Aria: Yes — mesh coordinates credential sources and emits hooks; it does not alter transport retry semantics unless you opt into the provided Retry/Circuit preset.

Lena Holt: The iterator pool reduces allocations, but do we risk reuse of stale buffers across streams?
Aria: Pool handles are zeroed and validated on checkout. We added tests that fuzz concurrent checkout/return and added a sanitizer in debug builds.

Marco Nguyen: CI flaked on the first integration run — what mitigations?
Aria: Increased job timeout and added a small jitter to the integration replay to avoid time-aligned probes; rerun passed.

Priya Desai: Docs look good; please add a short example showing migration for custom retry profiles.
Aria: Added an examples/streaming/failover-demo and snippet in docs showing how to wrap existing retry profile with the mesh adapter.

Final: Approved by Samir, Lena, Marco; merged after squash.
